disagreements.topic: Whether the CEO's 2026 share sales were under a Rule 10b5-1 plan
disagreements.positions: The round-1 supervisor said the CEO's March and June 2026 sales were made under a 10b5-1 plan adopted Mar 3 2026 (it cited a MarketScreener summary). In round 2, agent_3 disagrees, citing the primary Form 4s and Form 144s. The other agents accepted the round-1 correction or did not address it.
disagreements.resolution: agent_3 is right, and the round-1 supervisor's correction was wrong. All of CEO Arash Adam Foroughi's Form 4s for the Mar 11-12 and Jun 10-12 2026 sales have the Rule 10b5-1 box set to false, and none has a plan footnote. His June Form 144s leave the plan-adoption date blank. The Mar 3 2026 plan in the Q1 10-Q belongs to director Maynard Webb (up to 40,000 shares), not to the CEO, and the 10-Q says no other officer or director adopted a plan that quarter. So the CEO's sales (about $51m in June: $14.6m on Jun 10, $25.3m on Jun 11 and $11.2m on Jun 12 at $473.55-516.51, plus March sales) were discretionary open-window sales, made inside the class period (Feb 12-Aug 5 2026). This strengthens the class action's scienter argument a little. It has no direct effect on earnings, so it does not move the ladder.

drivers.derivation: Q3 FY2026 actual 2,184.8 (+55.5% y/y). Q4 FY2026 2491.4: guide mid $2,380M x (1 + 4.68%), the median of the five-quarter guide record (+5.6/+4.6/+4.7/-0.3/+5.5%; guidance_check); the pre-print +1% haircut was the main Q3 error. FY2027-29 built from the two demand engines (not disclosed separately; one revenue driver): revenue = installs x net revenue per install (10-Q MD&A: Q3 installs +2%, NRPI +55%; Q2 -2%/+58%; Q1 -18%/+93%; FY2025 +3%/+72%; src 47, 2, 3, 16), i.e. growth is pricing of deeper-funnel installs by Axon and new consumer advertisers, not install volume. SPLIT (estimate, not disclosed; CFO Q3 call: no split given, src 51): gaming ~84% / consumer ~16% of FY2026 revenue, triangulated from the Q3 call: total +55.5% y/y (src 46) with consumer 'triple digits' taken at ~+110% (low end; Kilian 2026-11-05) and gaming 'nearly 50%' taken at 47-49% puts consumer at ~14-18% of Q3-26 revenue (gaming +49% -> 14%, +48% -> 16%, +47% -> 18%), centre 16%; Q1 lower and the Q4 peak higher (src 51). The Q1-26 call's '$1 billion run rate a year ago' (src 49) is not stated as revenue or advertiser spend; APP reports net revenue ('net revenue dollars', gross spend near $20B annualized vs ~$8.7B revenue, src 51), so it is not used for the split. Sensitivity below. GAMING: end market flat (mobile game IAP $82B, +1% in 2025, Sensor Tower, src 50); APP grows by share and per-install pricing. Q3-26 gaming grew 'nearly 50%' y/y with the next-generation model only partly rolled out; the rest of the transition is ahead but with no committed cadence (CEO, src 51). Management's earlier gaming expectation was 20-30% a year with law-of-large-numbers drag (analyst recap, Q3 call; CEO Q1-26 call 'way over' it every quarter, src 49, 51); the CEO now commits only to ~30% for the whole business and says gaming 'could' grow faster if the new model is optimized (src 51). Path: +30% FY2027 (top of the earlier range: the rollout completes in 1H27 and laps the Q3-26 step by 2H27), +25% FY2028, +20% FY2029 (bottom of the range by then, against a flat IAP market). CONSUMER (web/e-commerce): advertiser spend 'growing triple digits' y/y and 'double digits' q/q in Q3-26 (CFO, src 51); self-serve opened in June 2026, rolled out in sequence with mid-market first (Q1-26 and Q2-26 calls, src 49, 17); customers mostly Western, international effort not yet launched (src 49); new customers ~$70k a year with near-zero churn after 30 days (src 49); CEO Q3: 'really early', 'lightly penetrated', new-customer acquisition now a growth component, the new model helps most where data is sparse, 'exactly where our consumer vertical lives' (src 51); still slow to ramp: incrementality studies, SMB 'further into the future' (src 51). Path +75% / +50% / +35%: a step down from 2026's triple digits each year as the base grows, held up by new customers and international. Total 11,583 / 15,070 / 18,615 (+37.2% / +30.1% / +23.5%). Consumer share 10% / 20% instead of 16%: -3.4% / +2.3% on value; with the 16% start consumer is ~20% / 24% / 26% of FY2027-29 revenue. Whole-business path FY2026-29 compounds at +30.1% a year, in line with management's 'roughly 30% annually over the long term' (src 51) and below its 'run well ahead' aim. Quarters: y/y declining linearly within each year, solved to hit each year's total (Q2 seasonally weakest, Q4 peak, src 17); Q1-27 +4.8% q/q vs +11% in Q1-26 and +16% in Q1-25, as the consumer mix brings 'tougher Q1s' after Q4 (src 51). Alternative on Kilian's card: gaming +20% a year (bottom of the earlier range) and consumer cut to +50/40/30%, FY2027 +24.8%, FY2026-29 +23.6% a year.
